findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows an underground electric line entry point from Valley View Road on the western boundary, but does not include an explicit label or designation identifying this as the 'Point of Service' (POS) per UCM § 1.3.4. The plan shows transformer pads and meters but no specific POS location marker. Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows a single transformer pad labeled 'Transformer Pad (Typ.)' without identifying which location serves as the point of service connection to Austin Energy infrastructure. Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) shows only overhead electric lines along the boundary, with no POS designation. Per UCM § 1.4.2.6 Table 1.4.3.B, the POS must be shown on the site plan showing all utilities, landscape plan, and all electrical plans.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(6) requires that the point of electric service be shown on plan sheets. UCM § 1.3.4 defines POS as 'the location where Austin Energy's and the Customer's conductors are connected or terminated.' The presence of transformer pads and underground line routing does not constitute a clear POS designation. Without an explicit label identifying which location serves as the official POS, the requirement is not met. The applicant must clearly designate the POS location on all required sheets per UCM § 1.4.2.6.
findings.comment: Point of service location is not explicitly marked or labeled on any of the required plan sheets. The plans show electrical infrastructure (transformers, meters, underground lines) but do not identify the specific point where Austin Energy's infrastructure connects to the customer's electrical system. The POS must be clearly designated on the site plan showing all utilities, landscape plan, and all electrical plans per UCM § 1.4.2.6.

findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows underground electric line routing with '-E-' markings labeled 'Underground Electric Line,' routing from the western boundary through the site with pull boxes and connections to transformer pads. However, Sheet 9 (Site Plan showing all utilities) shows only a single transformer pad location without showing the underground routing from the source to the buildings or between transformers. Sheet 19 (Utility Tap Plan) contains legend symbols for 'Proposed Underground Electric' but these symbols are NOT actually drawn anywhere on the plan - the plan shows water, wastewater, and storm drain routing but zero electric line routing. Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) shows only the overhead electric line along the southern boundary with no underground electric cabling shown. Per UCM § 1.4.2.6 Table 1.4.3.B, underground electric cabling routing must be shown on the site plan showing all utilities, landscape plan, and utility plans.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.4.2.6 requires that 'Customer Drawings Specifications' include the site plan showing all utilities, landscaping plan, and all electrical plans with appropriate detail. The requirement applies to showing underground electric cabling routing, conduit locations, and service lines from the source to the development and within the site. While Sheet 21 shows routing details, the required sheets per Table 1.4.3.B are incomplete: Sheet 9 (Site Plan) omits the routing details shown on Sheet 21; Sheet 19 (Utility Tap Plan) has legend symbols but NO actual electric routing depicted; Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) shows only overhead electric, not underground routing. The inconsistency means the site plan showing all utilities does not adequately convey underground electric routing as required.
findings.comment: Underground electric cabling routing is shown on the Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21) but is missing or incomplete on other required plan sheets. Sheet 19 (Utility Tap Plan) contains legend symbols for underground electric but these symbols are not actually used in the drawing area. Underground electric routing must be consistently shown on the site plan showing all utilities (Sheet 9), landscape plan (Sheet 31), and utility plans (Sheet 19) per UCM § 1.4.2.6 Table 1.4.3.B.

findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows two pad-mounted transformer pads clearly labeled 'Electrical Transformer Pad' located on the western side (between western property line and buildings) and eastern side (between eastern property line and buildings) of the site. Sheet 9 (Site Plan showing all utilities) shows only one transformer pad labeled 'Transformer Pad (Typ.)' on the western side of the site, but does not identify the second transformer pad shown on Sheet 21. Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) shows no transformer pads or locations marked. Per UCM § 1.4.2.6 Table 1.4.3.B, transformer locations must be shown on the site plan showing all utilities, landscape plan, and all electrical plans.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.4.2.6 specifies that all electrical plans and the site plan showing all utilities must depict transformer locations. Sheet 21 documents two transformers, but Sheet 9 (the official Site Plan showing all utilities) shows only one transformer location. Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) shows no transformers at all. The inconsistency between sheets means that the required plan sheets do not comprehensively show all transformer locations as required. The discrepancy between one transformer shown on Sheet 9 and two shown on Sheet 21 must be clarified, and all transformer locations must be depicted on all required sheets.
findings.comment: Transformer pads are shown on the Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21) with two pads identified, but the Site Plan showing all utilities (Sheet 9) shows only one transformer pad, and the Landscape Plan (Sheet 31) shows none. Transformer locations must be clearly shown on all required plan sheets per UCM § 1.4.2.6. Clarify the number and location of transformers and ensure they are depicted on the site plan showing all utilities, landscape plan, and all electrical plans.

findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows multiple locations labeled 'Electrical Meters' on the exterior walls of various buildings (visible on north walls of Buildings 1, 3, and 4; south walls of Buildings 2, 7, and 8) indicating meter banks or grouped meters. However, Sheet 9 (Site Plan showing all utilities) does not show or label any electric meter locations on any of the building footprints. Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) shows no meter locations marked. Per UCM § 1.4.2.6 Table 1.4.3.B, electric meter locations must be shown on the site plan showing all utilities, landscape plan, and all electrical plans.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.3.4 defines the Point of Service (POS) and per UCM § 1.4.2.6 Table 1.4.3.B, all electrical plans and the site plan showing all utilities must depict meter locations. While Sheet 21 shows meter callouts indicating meter locations on buildings, the required sheets per the standard (Site Plan showing all utilities and Landscape Plan) do not indicate where meters are located. Sheet 9 and Sheet 31 fail to show meter locations, creating incomplete documentation of this required infrastructure element.
findings.comment: Electric meter locations are shown on the Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21) but are missing from the Site Plan showing all utilities (Sheet 9) and the Landscape Plan (Sheet 31). Electric meter locations must be clearly marked on all required plan sheets per UCM § 1.4.2.6 Table 1.4.3.B.

findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows pull boxes labeled 'Electrical Pull Box' at multiple locations along the underground electric routing. Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) shows possible utility poles (cross-mark symbols) along the overhead electric line on the southern boundary, but these are not explicitly labeled as poles. Sheet 9 (Site Plan) does not show any poles or service drops marked or labeled. Per the project's 'Preliminary Electrical Design Plan' title and visual analysis, the internal site service is underground (no new poles or overhead drops within the site boundaries shown), but Sheet 9 and Sheet 31 do not adequately depict the utility poles that may serve the existing overhead electric line on the southern boundary or any service drop infrastructure.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.4.2.6 requires that poles or service drops be shown on required plan sheets. While Sheet 21 shows pull boxes (dry infrastructure), and Sheet 31 may show existing poles via symbols, the required sheets (Site Plan showing all utilities and Landscape Plan per Table 1.4.3.B) do not clearly label or identify poles and service drops. The pull boxes shown on Sheet 21 must also be depicted on the Site Plan showing all utilities (Sheet 9) to meet the requirement of consistent infrastructure documentation across all required sheets.
findings.comment: Poles or service drops are not clearly shown and labeled on the required plan sheets. While pull boxes are shown on the Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21), utility poles along existing overhead electric lines are not explicitly marked on the Site Plan (Sheet 9) or Landscape Plan (Sheet 31). All poles and service drop infrastructure must be clearly identified on the site plan showing all utilities and landscape plan per UCM § 1.4.2.6.

findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows underground electric line routing with labeled callouts for 'Underground Electric Line' and pull boxes, but does not include specifications for cable sizes or conduit dimensions. The grouping definition states that duct bank requirements 'cannot be determined from plans alone' and require Austin Energy Design confirmation through ESPA documentation or Letter of Agreement. No cable size specifications, conduit sizing (such as '5-inch conduit' or '1000 MCM cables'), or main line distribution designations are visible on Sheet 21. The supplementary documents (Master Comment Report, Engineer's Summary Letter) do not reference duct bank requirements or main line distribution infrastructure.
findings.reasoning: Per the grouping's own regulatory overview, duct bank determination 'cannot be definitively determined from site plan sheets alone' and requires AE Design confirmation based on service voltage, load, and distribution system design. The applicability of this checklist item depends on Austin Energy Design determining whether duct banks are required, which would be documented in ESPA documentation or a Letter of Agreement for Underground Electric Service. Without access to AE Design documentation confirming duct bank requirements, the status cannot be definitively determined to be fail. However, if duct banks ARE required per AE Design, they are not shown on the plans.
findings.comment: Duct bank routing and locations cannot be verified from available site plan sheets. Whether duct banks are required must be confirmed through Austin Energy ESPA documentation, Letter of Agreement, or utility coordination notes. If duct banks are determined to be required, they must be shown on the electrical site plan and cross-referenced on the site plan showing all utilities and landscape plan.

findings.observation: The site plan shows the development abuts Valley View Road to the west. Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows street frontage along Valley View Road and references street improvement requirements in the general notes ('For construction within the right-of-way, a ROW excavation permit is required'). Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) shows a street yard area along Valley View Road (labeled with H.2 'STREET YARD' symbol). Neither Sheet 9 nor Sheet 31 shows any street lighting layout, light pole locations, or street lighting infrastructure marked or labeled. The project appears to include public street frontage triggering street lighting applicability per UCM § 1.6.0, which directs customers to 'contact AE Design' for specific requirements. No indication of street lighting coordination or requirements is present in the visible plans.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.6.0 addresses Street Lighting requirements. The grouping's applicability guidance states street lighting applies when 'site includes or abuts public streets requiring street lighting.' This site has frontage on Valley View Road (a local street per facts.md), which would typically require street lighting evaluation. The grouping notes that 'specific street lighting requirements are determined by contacting AE Design' and the applicant should verify coordination with AE Design. The absence of any street lighting layout or infrastructure markings on Sheets 9 and 31 (the Site Plan and Landscape Plan where street lighting must be shown per UCM § 1.4.2.6) constitutes non-compliance unless AE Design has waived street lighting for this project. Documentation of AE Design waiver or determination is not visible in available documents.
findings.comment: Street lighting layout and light pole locations are not shown on the Site Plan (Sheet 9) or Landscape Plan (Sheet 31), though the site has public street frontage on Valley View Road. If street lighting is required per Austin Energy Design determination, the layout and pole locations must be shown on the site plan and landscape plan per UCM § 1.4.2.6. Confirm with AE Design whether street lighting is required for this project and provide documentation of the determination.

findings.observation: No street lighting conduit plan, conduit routing, or conduit connections are shown on any of the reviewed sheets (Sheet 9, 21, or 31). The Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21) shows only building service conduit routing and meter connections, with no separate street lighting conduit layer or specifications. Sheets 9 and 31 show no lighting conduit markings. Per UCM § 1.4.2.6 Table 1.4.3.B, if street lighting is required, the conduit plan must be shown on the site plan, landscape plan, and all electrical plans.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.6.0 governs Street Lighting. If street lighting is applicable to this project (site has Valley View Road frontage per facts.md), then the street light conduit plan, connections, and routing must be shown per UCM § 1.4.2.6 Table 1.4.3.B on the site plan, landscape plan, and all electrical plans. The complete absence of street lighting conduit documentation on all sheets constitutes a deficiency if street lighting is required. This must be confirmed with AE Design and, if required, the conduit plans must be added.
findings.comment: Street light conduit plan, conduit connections, and routing are not shown on any of the required plan sheets (Site Plan, Landscape Plan, Electrical Plans). If street lighting is required for this project, complete conduit plans must be provided per UCM § 1.4.2.6 Table 1.4.3.B. Confirm street lighting requirements with Austin Energy Design.

findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows building identifications, unit counts, and floor areas, but does not include any notation of projected electrical load (in kW, kVA, amps, or other standard electrical load units) for the development or individual buildings. Sheet 9 (Site Plan) does not show projected electrical load. No other sheets reference electrical load calculations or projections. The supplementary documents reviewed (Engineer's Summary Letter, Master Comment Report) do not mention electrical load.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(6) requires that the 'projected electrical load' be shown on plan sheets submitted for Austin Energy land development review. This is a fundamental requirement to demonstrate the adequacy of service and determine whether line extension or other infrastructure upgrades are needed. The absence of any projected load notation on the electrical design plan is a direct non-compliance with this UCM requirement.
findings.comment: Projected electrical load is not shown on any plan sheets. UCM § 1.16.0(6) requires documentation of the projected electrical load for the development. Add load calculations and clearly indicate the total projected load and individual building loads on the electrical site plan and other required sheets.

findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows two pad-mounted transformer pads labeled 'Electrical Transformer Pad' but does not indicate whether electrical service pedestals are required or planned for this development. UCM § 1.5.3.4 establishes that electrical pedestals may be used for 'residential lots up to 200 amp maximum underground services' per optional policy. However, this is a multi-family townhome development (39 units in 8 buildings), not traditional residential lots, and pedestals would typically not apply to multi-family service. The applicability of this item depends on whether Austin Energy Design has determined that pedestals are required for the service type selected for this development.
findings.reasoning: The grouping definition states this item applies 'Only when electrical pedestals are required for service' and requires checking 'Austin Energy Design documentation, Letter of Agreement, or utility coordination notes specifying pedestal service.' Without access to AE Design documentation confirming pedestal service is required for this multi-family development, the status cannot be definitively determined. Pedestals are typically used for single-family or small residential lots with limited service capacity (≤200 amps), not multi-family buildings with distributed service. If pedestals ARE required per AE Design, they should be shown on the plans.
findings.comment: Electrical service pedestals are not shown on the Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21), which instead shows pad-mounted transformers. Whether pedestals are required must be confirmed through Austin Energy Design documentation or Letter of Agreement. For a multi-family development of this scale, pad-mounted transformers appear more appropriate, but final service type determination requires AE Design confirmation.

findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) indicates underground electric service ('Underground Electric Line' label) and shows the internal routing. However, the plan does not include any callouts, notes, or designations showing trenching assignments (which party is responsible for trenching and at what depths). Per UCM § 1.5.3.4, the 'customer is responsible for trenching' for underground electric work, but the plan does not include notes or specifications assigning trenching responsibilities or depths to the contractor/customer.
findings.reasoning: The grouping definition states this item applies 'Only when underground electric work is required' and notes that 'Customer responsible for trenching per UCM § 1.5.3.4, but specific plan documentation requirement is operational practice.' Since underground electric service is clearly required (shown on Sheet 21), and trenching will be necessary, the lack of specific trenching assignment notes on the plan represents incomplete design documentation. However, this is noted as an 'operational practice' rather than a codified requirement, making determination difficult. If present, trenching assignments should include depth specifications, material specifications, and responsibility assignments.
findings.comment: Trenching assignments and responsibilities are not indicated on the Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21). While customer trenching responsibility is established in UCM § 1.5.3.4 for underground work, the plans should include notes specifying trenching depths, materials, and construction responsibilities to ensure proper coordination with the contractor.

findings.observation: The Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21) shows electrical infrastructure (transformers, underground lines, meters) but does not include any indication of whether natural gas service is required for the development or identify which site components (if any) will use gas service. The Site Plan (Sheet 9) shows water and wastewater utilities but does not address gas service. The Engineer's Summary Letter (supplementary document) discusses only water and wastewater utilities, with no mention of gas service requirements or coordination with gas providers. There is no notation on any sheet indicating whether this multi-family townhome development will include gas service for heating, cooking, hot water, or other building systems.
findings.reasoning: The grouping definition establishes that checklist item EL-17.15 applies to 'All sites' and requires the plans to 'indicate whether gas service is required or identify which site components will use gas service.' This is a general site requirement under Reviewer Convention. The complete absence of any reference to gas service documentation on any plan sheets constitutes non-compliance. Multi-family townhomes typically require gas service for heating and hot water, and this coordination must be documented.
findings.comment: Plans do not indicate whether natural gas service is required or identify which site components will use gas service. Add notation to the site plan and utility plans indicating gas service requirements and which buildings or building systems will use natural gas (e.g., unit heating, hot water systems).

findings.observation: The Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21) shows underground electric line routing entering the site from Valley View Road on the west side, but does not include any notation indicating whether a line extension from Austin Energy's existing infrastructure is required. The supplementary documents (Master Comment Report referencing Austin Energy Design Criteria, Bluebeam link to AE comments) suggest that Austin Energy has reviewed the project, but the specific comments regarding line extension determination are not accessible in the available documents. The grouping definition explicitly states that 'whether line extension is required (vs. Service-Only service) cannot be determined from site plan features alone - this determination is made by AE Design based on existing infrastructure capacity and location.'
findings.reasoning: Per the grouping definition, 'Line extension' determination cannot be made from site plan analysis alone and requires 'Austin Energy ESPA approval letters, Letter of Agreement for Underground Electric Service, or utility coordination notes stating line extension requirement and costs.' The presence of underground line routing on Sheet 21 could indicate either a service-only installation (connecting to existing nearby AE infrastructure) or a line extension (new AE infrastructure required). Without AE Design documentation (ESPA, Letter of Agreement, or utility coordination notes), the status cannot be definitively determined. The applicant must provide AE Design determination documentation.
findings.comment: Whether electric line extension is required cannot be determined from the site plan alone. This determination must be made by Austin Energy Design based on existing infrastructure capacity and location. Provide Austin Energy ESPA approval documentation, Letter of Agreement for Underground Electric Service, or utility coordination notes confirming whether line extension is required and any associated costs or conditions.

findings.observation: Sheet 21 of the primary site plan is titled 'Preliminary Electrical Design Plan,' which suggests this may be a preliminary or partial electrical design. However, this is the only electrical infrastructure sheet visible in the 39-sheet primary site plan set. There is no evidence of a separate, detailed 'Electric Site Plan' document submitted to the AB+C portal as an additional submittal beyond the primary site plan. The grouping definition states that an electric site plan 'is required as separate submittal' only when determined to be required by 'Project complexity, Austin Energy coordination notes, and submittal requirements.' The absence of evidence of a separate electric site plan submittal suggests either (1) it has not been submitted, or (2) Austin Energy has not required it as a separate document for this project.
findings.reasoning: The applicability of EL-17.17 is conditional: 'Only when electric site plan is required as separate submittal.' The determination requires checking 'Project complexity, Austin Energy coordination notes, and submittal requirements for the development type.' Sheet 21 is labeled 'Preliminary,' which may indicate incompleteness or serve as a placeholder for a more detailed electric site plan. Without clear evidence that Austin Energy has required a separate detailed electric site plan for this project (vs. accepting the electrical design as part of Sheet 21 of the primary site plan), and without access to the full Austin Energy coordination notes (Bluebeam link), a definitive determination cannot be made. However, the 'Preliminary' designation suggests this may not constitute a complete electric site plan.
findings.comment: A 'Preliminary' Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21) is included in the site plan set, but it is unclear whether a complete, detailed Electric Site Plan has been submitted as a separate document or whether Austin Energy has accepted this preliminary sheet as adequate. Confirm with Austin Energy whether a more detailed separate Electric Site Plan submittal is required for this project. If required, provide the detailed electrical site plan as a separate document in the AB+C portal.

findings.observation: Facts.md identifies several plat-dedicated electrical easements that should be shown on the site plan: 'Easement 7 & 8 — 5' Electric Easements (×2)' from Travis County Doc 73/76 (Mecey Subdivision plat). These are dedicated easements recorded in the subdivision plat. Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) and Sheet 9 (Site Plan) do not show these dedicated electrical easements with dimensions and extents clearly delineated. Sheet 9 does reference '5' Elec. & Tele. Easement' and 'Electric Easement' in vision analysis observations, but the specific dimensions, locations, and extents of the two 5-foot electric easements from the plat are not clearly dimensioned or highlighted.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(1)(i) requires that 'electrical easements' be shown on the plans. The grouping definition states 'Check: Verify all public and private electrical easements (existing and proposed) are shown with dimensions and extents.' Facts.md confirms the existence of two plat-dedicated 5-foot electric easements from the Mecey Subdivision recorded plat. The site plan must clearly show these easements with their dimensions and extents clearly marked. While Sheet 9 may reference these easements, the vision analysis indicates they are not clearly dimensioned or consistently depicted across sheets.
findings.comment: Electrical easement locations and extents are not clearly delineated with dimensions on the site plan. The two plat-dedicated 5-foot electric easements from the Mecey Subdivision (Travis County Doc 73/76) must be clearly shown with exact dimensions and extents on the site plan and electrical plans per UCM § 1.16.0(1)(i). Ensure all existing and proposed electrical easements are clearly dimensioned on the plans.

findings.observation: The vision analysis of Sheet 9 (Site Plan) identified 'existing electric facilities and easements along the boundaries' including 'An Overhead Electric line, marked by the linetype "- OHE -", runs along the entire southern property boundary' and 'An easement labeled "5' Elec. & Tele. Easement" is noted near the bottom right (southeast) corner' and 'An easement labeled "Electric Easement" is noted along the eastern property line boundary.' However, the site plan does not show specific identification of existing Austin Energy infrastructure such as utility pole numbers, transformer identification, guy wire locations, anchor points, or the locations and identifications of existing distribution structures. Facts.md does not list any existing AE facilities recorded in the property description, suggesting existing AE infrastructure is limited to the boundary easements and overhead line.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(1)(ii) requires showing 'existing AE infrastructure' and the grouping definition specifies 'Verify all existing AE transmission/distribution structures, poles, guys, anchors, and transformers are shown with accurate locations.' While the overhead electric line and easements along the southern and eastern boundaries are referenced on Sheet 9, the specific existing AE facilities (such as utility pole locations, pole numbers, or transformer identification) are not clearly marked with locations and identifications. For the existing overhead electric line along the southern boundary, the specific utility poles supporting that line should be identified and located on the site plan.
findings.comment: Existing electric facilities (Austin Energy transmission/distribution structures, poles, guys, anchors, transformers) are not clearly shown and identified on the site plan. While an existing overhead electric line runs along the southern property boundary per the site plan, the specific utility pole locations and pole numbers supporting that line are not clearly marked. All existing Austin Energy facilities on or adjacent to the site must be shown with accurate locations per UCM § 1.16.0(1)(ii).

findings.observation: A comprehensive review of the 39-sheet primary site plan set and supplementary documents shows no One-Line Diagram of the electrical riser included. Sheet 21 is titled 'Preliminary Electrical Design Plan' and shows electrical infrastructure (transformers, meters, underground lines, pull boxes), but does not include a one-line riser diagram showing the electrical system architecture, service entrance, main disconnect, panel configuration, branch circuits, or electrical load flow. No separate electrical riser diagram or one-line diagram document appears in the supplementary documents (Engineer's Summary Letter, Master Comment Report, etc.).
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.4.2.6 Table 1.4.3.B explicitly requires as a 'Required Plan Sheet': 'One-Line Diagram of the electrical riser.' This is a fundamental requirement for the complete electrical design submittal. The absence of this diagram constitutes non-compliance with the standard. A one-line diagram must show the system architecture from the point of service, through the main service equipment, to the distribution panels serving the individual units, clearly showing voltages, amperage ratings, and major circuit configurations.
findings.comment: One-Line Diagram of the electrical riser is not included in the plan set. UCM § 1.4.2.6 Table 1.4.3.B requires this diagram as a required plan sheet. Provide a complete One-Line Diagram showing the electrical system architecture, service entrance, main disconnect, voltage/amperage ratings, and distribution to building service panels.

findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows underground electric line routing, transformer pad locations, and meter locations but does not include clearance dimensions between buildings, permanent structures (retaining walls, fences), other utilities (water, wastewater, storm drain lines), and the electric facilities. The vision analysis of Sheet 21 noted 'Because this is a 2D plan view without depths or profile details provided on this sheet, vertical conflicts or clearance issues cannot be definitively assessed, though numerous horizontal crossing points are evident.' Sheet 19 (Utility Tap Plan) shows water, wastewater, and storm drain crossing electric line locations but does not provide clearance dimensions. No profile sheets showing vertical clearances between electric lines and other utilities are evident in the sheet index.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(2) requires that plans 'demonstrate sufficient clearances for existing and proposed electric facilities.' The requirement is to show 'Clearance dimensions shown for buildings, permanent structures, and other utilities relative to electric facilities.' The absence of clearance callouts and dimensions on the electrical plan (Sheet 21) constitutes non-compliance. At minimum, where underground electric lines cross or run parallel to water, wastewater, and storm drain lines, the clearance dimensions (vertical separation) must be clearly shown. Profile views or cross-sections may be required to demonstrate adequate vertical separation.
findings.comment: Plans do not demonstrate sufficient clearances for existing and proposed electric facilities. The Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21) does not include clearance dimensions between the underground electric lines and buildings, permanent structures, or other utilities (water, wastewater, storm drain). Add clearance callouts and dimensions to the electrical site plan, and provide profile or cross-section views where electric lines cross other utilities to demonstrate compliance with applicable clearance standards.

findings.observation: The requirements for CAD file georeferencing to NAD 83 Texas Central Zone 4203 cannot be verified from the visual site plan sheets alone. The grouping file specifies that CAD files must be 'georeferenced to NAD 83 Texas Central Zone 4203 coordinate system' per UCM § 1.4.2.6. However, the available site plan documents are presented as PDF or image files, not the underlying CAD files. To verify georeferencing, access to the actual .dwg (AutoCAD) files and their coordinate system settings would be required.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.4.2.6 requires that 'AutoCAD files (georeferenced: NAD 83 Texas Central Zone 4203)' be submitted. The verification of CAD georeferencing cannot be accomplished through visual analysis of the site plan sheets; it requires examination of the CAD file metadata and coordinate system settings. This review methodology focuses on site plan sheet content analysis, which does not provide visibility into CAD file properties. The applicant must provide confirmation of CAD file georeferencing by submitting the files with proper coordinate system settings, or by providing a certification that the files are properly georeferenced.
findings.comment: CAD file georeferencing to NAD 83 Texas Central Zone 4203 cannot be verified from available site plan image/PDF files. Provide the original AutoCAD (.dwg) files or a written certification from the engineer confirming that all CAD files are properly georeferenced to NAD 83 Texas Central Zone 4203 coordinate system per UCM § 1.4.2.6.
